environment.scope: Finite browser host with virtual Rust applets. Node ABI and Chromium project worker/main-thread controls are separate measurements. No OS applets, providers, native pipes, native/Bash comparison or cold-start/memory claim.

final_node.method: Actual preserved release WASM modules, instantiated before timing, serial 3 alternating rounds, 20 warmups then40batches of5 operations. Node operation includes JSON request encode/ABI/Rust/response JSON decode. Chromium operation is the existing worker elapsed clock; roundtrip includes postMessage and scheduling but excludes Playwright evaluation transport. Every batch final response checked against a complete cross-binary hash plus independent output/call-count/FS/trace-cap/UTF8-escaping byte-budget oracles; warmups and fixture/hash checking excluded from timing. Browser clock quantized; batch averages retained, not zero latency. No builds/tests concurrent. No native/OS commands/provider calls; not cold start, memory or Bash comparison.

limits: All profiling serial, no concurrent builds/tests/stress. Warm WASM modules; compile/instantiate/fetch setup excluded. Background activity uncontrolled.

Full request/response hashes match across all reports; independent exact stdout/call-count/FS/cwd/trace-count/escaped UTF8 byte-budget oracles. Every timed batch final response checked; fixtures are pure and repeat identically.

Browser worker source and ABI served locally, without UI rendering. Worker elapsed includes JSON encode/ABI/Rust/decode; roundtrip also includes postMessage cloning/scheduling, excludes Playwright evaluation transport.

Per-request small worker medians were quantized at10us/20us (+100% ratio); do not interpret this as a precise gain/regression. Roundtrip40us unchanged. Separate500-operation browser-main-thread ABI batches resolve tiny timings, about9.7%lower, and exclude worker/RPC.
Pure JSON median controls approximately flat; one earlier worker round varies60us->80us. Retain all samples; no unedited-path speedup claim.
WASM grows909bytes(~0.175%); startup/compile latency, allocation/RSS/peak memory and native-runtime performance unmeasured. Native CLI binary remains byte-identical.
